subject.title: [Feature]: [Feature Request] 按用户维度统计 Token 使用量

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class per-user usage accounting inside core, and what identity boundary should define a user?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but solving it changes identity, privacy, storage, authorization, and quota/billing semantics in a project whose documented Gateway model is single-operator by default.

options.title: Core identity accounting
options.body: Define the user identity, authorized readers, storage schema, aggregation RPCs, Dashboard and `/usage` behavior, and privacy/retention rules before implementation.

options.title: Plugin or external reporting first
options.body: Keep core usage as session/agent/channel/model/provider aggregates and let a plugin or export pipeline build user billing reports until the core identity model is approved.

options.title: No multi-user accounting
options.body: Keep OpenClaw's single-operator model and narrow future work to existing session, agent, and model usage improvements.

recommendation.title: Core identity accounting
recommendation.body: Define the user identity, authorized readers, storage schema, aggregation RPCs, Dashboard and `/usage` behavior, and privacy/retention rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest usage-surface and product-history evidence points to Peter Steinberger's cost-summary and usage infrastructure work.
